diagrams.title: 1 · How one validator votes
diagrams.scope: Paper rules and Agave vote checks

transitions.label: Start the slot
transitions.when: The validator starts this slot without a stored first vote.
transitions.action: Set the initial vote state to empty.
transitions.why: The validator must select one first vote for this slot.

transitions.label: Parent condition false
transitions.when: A complete block arrives, but its parent does not meet the vote condition.
transitions.action: Keep the block for another check.
transitions.why: The validator must not support a child before it has the required parent evidence.

transitions.label: Parent condition true
transitions.when: A complete valid block arrives. Its parent meets the condition. No first vote exists.
transitions.action: Send NotarVote for B.
transitions.why: The block extends a chain that this validator can support under the protocol rules.

transitions.label: Parent condition true
transitions.when: ParentReady or a parent vote permits a new check. The stored block now meets the condition.
transitions.action: Send NotarVote for B. Remove the pending entry.
transitions.why: The missing parent evidence is now available. The block does not need to arrive again.

transitions.label: Keep waiting
transitions.when: A new check still finds insufficient parent evidence.
transitions.action: Keep the block and wait.
transitions.why: A new event alone does not make the block safe to support.

transitions.label: Skip this slot
transitions.when: A timeout or fallback handler calls trySkipWindow. This slot has no first vote.
transitions.action: Send SkipVote. Set Voted and BadWindow.
transitions.why: This vote helps the network continue to another leader window. One validator’s skip vote does not prove that the leader failed.

transitions.label: Skip the pending slot
transitions.when: The window skip function reaches this pending slot. The slot has no first vote.
transitions.action: Send SkipVote. Remove the pending entry.
transitions.why: The validator must not later send a different first vote when the missing parent evidence arrives.

transitions.label: Notar certificate for B
transitions.when: The validator has its own NotarVote for B and an ordinary notar certificate for B. BadWindow and ItsOver are false.
transitions.action: Send FinalVote for the slot. Set ItsOver.
transitions.why: The certificate proves 60% initial support. The final vote commits this validator to stop fallback support in this slot.

transitions.label: Safe fallback condition
transitions.when: SafeToSkip becomes true, or SafeToNotar becomes true for a block other than the original B.
transitions.action: Run trySkipWindow. Send the permitted fallback vote. Set BadWindow for the target slot.
transitions.why: The fallback condition excludes a conflicting fast-final result. The extra vote helps the network get a certificate and continue.

transitions.label: SafeToNotar for a block
transitions.when: SafeToNotar becomes true for block C after this validator sent an initial skip vote.
transitions.action: Run trySkipWindow. Send NotarFallbackVote for C.
transitions.why: The block now has sufficient evidence for fallback support. The validator can help make it a usable parent.

transitions.label: Another permitted fallback
transitions.when: A further fallback condition is true. The validator has not sent that fallback vote. ItsOver is false.
transitions.action: Send the permitted fallback vote after trySkipWindow.
transitions.why: Different fallback certificates can help resolve a failed leader window. The first vote remains fixed.

transitions.label: No new vote in this slot
transitions.when: A later event would otherwise cause another vote in this slot.
transitions.action: Do not send a new vote in this slot.
transitions.why: A final vote must remain a commitment. Reusing its stake for a conflicting fallback would break the finality argument.

diagrams.title: 2 · When a fallback vote is safe
diagrams.scope: Paper rules; Agave repair checks are identified below

transitions.label: Check block fallback
transitions.when: The validator has a first vote and new initial-vote information.
transitions.action: Check the SafeToNotar formula for each related block B.
transitions.why: The validator needs evidence that another block cannot fast-finalize before it adds fallback support for B.

transitions.label: Check skip fallback
transitions.when: The validator has a first vote and new initial-vote information.
transitions.action: Check the SafeToSkip formula.
transitions.why: Skip fallback is safe only when no block can get fast finality.

transitions.label: Block threshold met
transitions.when: The first-vote exclusion and one SafeToNotar threshold alternative are true.
transitions.action: Get B if its data is missing.
transitions.why: A vote that supports B must meet the paper’s data requirement. The data also identifies the parent.

transitions.label: Block available
transitions.when: The validator has block B.
transitions.action: Find its position in the leader window.
transitions.why: The first slot and later slots have different parent requirements.

transitions.label: First slot
transitions.when: B occupies the first slot of the leader window. The earlier checks passed.
transitions.action: Emit SafeToNotar for B.
transitions.why: The additional parent-certificate check for a later block in the same window does not apply here.

transitions.label: Later slot
transitions.when: B occupies a later slot in the leader window.
transitions.action: Wait for a notar-fallback certificate, or stronger evidence, for its parent.
transitions.why: A child must not receive fallback support without the required evidence for its parent.

transitions.label: Parent proof available
transitions.when: The required parent certificate is available.
transitions.action: Emit SafeToNotar for B.
transitions.why: Both the fallback threshold and the parent condition now hold.

transitions.label: Skip threshold met
transitions.when: The first vote was a notar vote. S + T - max N(B) is at least 40%.
transitions.action: Emit SafeToSkip for the slot.
transitions.why: The initial votes exclude fast finality for every block in the slot.

transitions.label: Consider block fallback
transitions.when: The handler receives SafeToNotar for B.
transitions.action: Run trySkipWindow. If ItsOver is false and the vote is new, send NotarFallbackVote for B.
transitions.why: The vote helps form a fallback certificate. The ItsOver check protects an earlier final-vote commitment.

transitions.label: Consider skip fallback
transitions.when: The handler receives SafeToSkip for the slot.
transitions.action: Run trySkipWindow. If ItsOver is false and the vote is new, send SkipFallbackVote.
transitions.why: The vote helps form a skip certificate. The ItsOver check protects an earlier final-vote commitment.

diagrams.title: 3 · What each certificate permits
diagrams.scope: Paper rules and Agave certificate processing

transitions.label: At least 80%
transitions.when: Initial notar votes for B reach at least 80% stake.
transitions.action: Build a fast-final certificate for B.
transitions.why: This threshold supplies enough correct initial support for the one-round finality proof.

transitions.label: At least 60%
transitions.when: Initial notar votes for B reach at least 60% stake.
transitions.action: Build an ordinary notar certificate for B.
transitions.why: The certificate proves initial support. It permits eligible validators to send final votes.

transitions.label: At least 60% distinct
transitions.when: Initial and fallback votes for B together cover at least 60% distinct stake.
transitions.action: Build a notar-fallback certificate for B.
transitions.why: The certificate allows B to serve as a parent when ordinary notar support was insufficient.

transitions.label: At least 60% distinct
transitions.when: Initial and fallback skip votes together cover at least 60% distinct stake.
transitions.action: Build a skip certificate.
transitions.why: The certificate permits a later leader to use a parent before this slot.

transitions.label: At least 60%
transitions.when: Final votes for the slot reach at least 60% stake.
transitions.action: Build a final certificate for the slot.
transitions.why: The certificate proves enough final-vote commitments for the two-round path.

transitions.label: Accept fast finality
transitions.when: The validator accepts a valid fast-final certificate for B.
transitions.action: Mark B as final.
transitions.why: The 80% certificate alone meets the one-round finality rule.

transitions.label: Try own final vote
transitions.when: The validator accepts an ordinary notar certificate for B.
transitions.action: Record BlockNotarized. Check the local final-vote conditions.
transitions.why: The certificate supplies the group evidence that a correct final voter needs.

transitions.label: Store notar proof
transitions.when: The validator accepts the notar certificate for B.
transitions.action: Use it with the final certificate, if that certificate is available.
transitions.why: The notar certificate identifies the block that the slot-only final certificate refers to.

transitions.label: Store final proof
transitions.when: The validator accepts the final certificate for the slot.
transitions.action: Use it with the ordinary notar certificate, if that certificate is available.
transitions.why: The final certificate proves commitments but does not contain the block identity by itself.

transitions.label: Accept two-round finality
transitions.when: Both valid certificates refer to the same slot. The notar certificate identifies B.
transitions.action: Mark B as final.
transitions.why: The pair supplies both block support and final-vote commitments.

transitions.label: Decide the earlier chain
transitions.when: Block B becomes final.
transitions.action: Finalize its ancestors. Decide omitted earlier slots as skips.
transitions.why: B identifies one parent chain. A final decision for B fixes that earlier chain.

transitions.label: Also meets fallback proof
transitions.when: An ordinary notar certificate already proves at least 60% support for B.
transitions.action: Treat that proof as sufficient for uses that need a notar-fallback certificate.
transitions.why: Initial notar votes are permitted inputs to a notar-fallback certificate.

transitions.label: Also meets notar proof
transitions.when: A fast-final certificate proves at least 80% initial notar stake.
transitions.action: Treat that evidence as meeting the weaker 60% notar requirement.
transitions.why: A group of at least 80% also meets a threshold of 60%.

transitions.label: Parent has enough support
transitions.when: The validator has a notar-fallback certificate, or stronger evidence, for B.
transitions.action: Check whether intervening slots have the required skip certificates.
transitions.why: A supported block can serve as a parent only when the next window can connect to it.

transitions.label: One more gap has proof
transitions.when: A new skip certificate arrives.
transitions.action: Check whether it completes the required sequence of skip certificates.
transitions.why: The next leader needs permission to pass every slot between its parent and its window.

diagrams.title: 4 · Why ParentReady permits a new window
diagrams.scope: Paper rules and Agave event handlers

transitions.label: Parent proof arrives
transitions.when: New certificate evidence for P arrives.
transitions.action: Check whether the certificate is sufficient for a parent.
transitions.why: A leader needs group support for the parent before normal block production can start.

transitions.label: Parent proof sufficient
transitions.when: P has a notar or notar-fallback certificate, or a stronger proof.
transitions.action: Check each intervening slot.
transitions.why: Support for P alone does not permit the leader to pass unsupported slots.

transitions.label: Parent proof absent
transitions.when: The validator lacks sufficient certificate evidence for P.
transitions.action: Keep the current evidence and wait.
transitions.why: The validator cannot yet declare P to be a permitted parent.

transitions.label: A skip proof is absent
transitions.when: At least one intervening slot lacks a skip certificate.
transitions.action: Wait for the missing certificate.
transitions.why: The leader needs permission to pass every slot in the gap.

transitions.label: A skip proof arrives
transitions.when: A new skip certificate arrives. The parent already has sufficient evidence.
transitions.action: Check the gap again.
transitions.why: Certificates can arrive in either order. The new certificate can complete the required evidence.

transitions.label: All required proofs exist
transitions.when: Every intervening slot has a skip certificate. This condition also holds when there are no intervening slots.
transitions.action: Record ParentReady(w,P).
transitions.why: The leader can now connect a new block to P with the required certificate evidence.

transitions.label: Retry pending votes
transitions.when: The validator records a new ready parent.
transitions.action: Check stored blocks again in slot order.
transitions.why: A stored block can now meet the parent condition that earlier prevented its initial notar vote.

transitions.label: Start timers once
transitions.when: This is the first ParentReady event for window w.
transitions.action: Start the window timers. Keep existing timers when more parents become ready.
transitions.why: The validator now has a reference time for leader progress. Later certificates must not postpone the deadlines indefinitely.

transitions.label: Prepare local parent state
transitions.when: Agave receives a ready parent above the local root.
transitions.action: Request the required replay-bank switch.
transitions.why: The validator needs the parent’s execution state to process blocks that extend that parent.

transitions.label: Start scheduled leader work
transitions.when: This validator leads the ready window, and Agave has not already passed that window.
transitions.action: Select a permitted parent. Send ProduceWindow to block creation.
transitions.why: The leader can produce a connected block now that the required evidence exists.

diagrams.title: 5 · Why timers cause skip votes
diagrams.scope: Paper deadlines and Agave crashed-leader check

transitions.label: First ParentReady
transitions.when: The validator gets the first ParentReady event for this window.
transitions.action: Set the first-data and block deadlines.
transitions.why: The event establishes when the validator can start to expect progress from this leader window.

transitions.label: First-data deadline
transitions.when: The first-data deadline expires.
transitions.action: Advance the timer machine to the first block deadline.
transitions.why: The validator must next find whether a complete block arrived in time.

transitions.label: Emit first-data event
transitions.when: The timer leaves the first-data wait state.
transitions.action: Emit TimeoutCrashedLeader for the first slot.
transitions.why: This event lets the vote handler check whether the leader has supplied any shred.

transitions.label: Emit block event
transitions.when: The deadline for block i expires.
transitions.action: Emit Timeout(i).
transitions.why: The vote handler must decide whether to stop its initial-vote wait for this slot.

transitions.label: More slots remain
transitions.when: A block deadline expires and another slot remains in the window.
transitions.action: Advance i by one. Add one block interval to the deadline.
transitions.why: Each successive block needs its own production interval.

transitions.label: Last deadline
transitions.when: The last block deadline in the window expires.
transitions.action: Finish this window’s timer machine.
transitions.why: There are no further slots to check in this window.

transitions.label: Check first data
transitions.when: The vote handler receives TimeoutCrashedLeader.
transitions.action: Check for an existing first vote and a first shred.
transitions.why: The handler must not treat a leader as silent when it already has data or a vote for the slot.

transitions.label: Check first vote
transitions.when: The vote handler receives Timeout(i).
transitions.action: Check whether the validator has a first vote for i.
transitions.why: The deadline can cause an initial skip only if the initial decision is still open.

transitions.label: No vote and no shred
transitions.when: The first-data deadline passed. No first vote or first shred exists for the first slot.
transitions.action: Run trySkipWindow.
transitions.why: The validator has no data evidence of progress and can help the network proceed to another window.

transitions.label: No first vote
transitions.when: The block deadline passed. The slot has no first vote.
transitions.action: Run trySkipWindow.
transitions.why: The validator did not get a block it could support before its deadline.

transitions.label: Vote or shred exists
transitions.when: The validator already has a first vote or a first shred for the slot.
transitions.action: Send no skip vote from this event.
transitions.why: An existing vote must remain fixed. A first shred makes the silence check insufficient, so the block deadline controls the later decision.

transitions.label: First vote exists
transitions.when: The validator already sent a first vote for this slot.
transitions.action: Keep that first vote.
transitions.why: A timeout cannot authorize a second initial vote.

diagrams.title: 6 · Why the leader keeps or changes its parent
diagrams.scope: Paper Algorithm 3 and the Agave feature gate

transitions.label: Start on expected parent
transitions.when: The preceding window’s last block is available. The feature and migration gates permit the early-start path.
transitions.action: Start the first block on expected parent P.
transitions.why: The leader can save certificate-wait time when P later becomes the ready parent.

transitions.label: Ready parent already known
transitions.when: ParentReady is available before the leader starts early work.
transitions.action: Build directly on the ready parent.
transitions.why: The required parent evidence already exists.

transitions.label: No ready parent yet
transitions.when: The leader still has no ParentReady notification.
transitions.action: Continue early slice production.
transitions.why: The work can be kept if the expected parent later becomes ready.

transitions.label: Ready parent arrives
transitions.when: The leader receives the selected ready parent Q.
transitions.action: Compare the full identity of Q with P.
transitions.why: A slot number alone does not identify a block. The leader must know whether its execution parent is correct.

transitions.label: Same parent
transitions.when: Q and P identify the same block.
transitions.action: Keep the existing first-block work.
transitions.why: The work already uses a permitted parent.

transitions.label: Different parent
transitions.when: Q and P identify different blocks.
transitions.action: Change the parent to Q and reset the first-block execution work.
transitions.why: The leader must build on a parent that meets ParentReady, even when its earlier expectation was wrong.

transitions.label: Continue on P
transitions.when: The existing parent has the required ready-parent evidence.
transitions.action: Produce the rest of the first block.
transitions.why: The leader can now complete normal production without a parent reset.

transitions.label: Continue on Q
transitions.when: The leader has changed to the permitted parent Q.
transitions.action: Produce the first block from the new parent state.
transitions.why: The final block must describe execution on Q, not on the discarded parent state.

transitions.label: First block complete
transitions.when: The first block is complete and another slot remains.
transitions.action: Use that block as the next block’s parent.
transitions.why: The next block must continue the same leader-window chain.

transitions.label: More window slots
transitions.when: The current block is complete and another slot remains in the window.
transitions.action: Produce the next block on the current block.
transitions.why: Successive parent links keep the produced blocks connected.

transitions.label: Last block complete
transitions.when: The leader completes the last block in its window.
transitions.action: End production for this window.
transitions.why: The leader schedule assigns the next window separately.

transitions.label: Window already passed
transitions.when: Agave finds that the requested production window is already unnecessary.
transitions.action: Do not start that window.
transitions.why: New production for a passed window cannot supply the work that the current window needs.

transitions.label: Network moved on
transitions.when: Agave receives WindowMovedOn during early production.
transitions.action: Stop the unnecessary work.
transitions.why: The leader must stop spending production time on a window that the network has passed.

diagrams.title: 7 · Why a final block can still need repair
diagrams.scope: Paper data rules and Agave local execution checks

transitions.label: All block data present
transitions.when: The validator has enough valid data to reconstruct the complete block.
transitions.action: Make B available for execution.
transitions.why: The validator cannot execute or check a complete block from insufficient data.

transitions.label: Execute the block
transitions.when: B and the required parent data are available.
transitions.action: Execute the parent chain and B.
transitions.why: The transactions need the parent’s state to produce the correct next state.

transitions.label: Replay complete
transitions.when: Agave completes replay and has the block ID.
transitions.action: Send Block(B) to the voting loop.
transitions.why: The current implementation checks execution before its normal initial notar vote.

transitions.label: Required data missing
transitions.when: A certificate or the fallback parent check requires block data that the validator lacks.
transitions.action: Request that specific block.
transitions.why: The certificate does not contain all transactions or the complete parent data.

transitions.label: Response absent or invalid
transitions.when: A repair request does not supply valid missing data.
transitions.action: Try another request to a sampled peer.
transitions.why: A faulty or unavailable peer must not find the repaired block’s contents.

transitions.label: Repair complete
transitions.when: Verified responses supply the required block data.
transitions.action: Make the block available for execution.
transitions.why: The validator now has the data identified by the block hash.

transitions.label: Final proof accepted
transitions.when: The validator verifies a fast-final certificate or the required pair of certificates.
transitions.action: Remember B as final. Request repair and check the local root conditions.
transitions.why: The validator must preserve the final decision even if local execution is not yet complete.

transitions.label: Final block data missing
transitions.when: The final block or its required ancestors are missing.
transitions.action: Request the missing data.
transitions.why: The validator needs that data before it can get the final block’s local state.

transitions.label: Check local conditions
transitions.when: The validator has a stored final decision for B.
transitions.action: Check the bank, block ID, vote history, and current root.
transitions.why: A valid finality proof alone does not establish that local execution is ready.

transitions.label: New replay result
transitions.when: A completed-block event arrives while final decisions are stored.
transitions.action: Check whether any final block can now become the local root.
transitions.why: Replay can supply the last missing local requirement after the certificate arrived.

transitions.label: A condition is false
transitions.when: At least one local root condition is false.
transitions.action: Keep the final decision and wait for the missing requirement.
transitions.why: The validator must not advance its local root to data or state it cannot yet use.

transitions.label: All conditions are true
transitions.when: A final block above the root meets every local requirement.
transitions.action: Select the highest eligible final block. Advance the root and remove unnecessary state.
transitions.why: The validator can now use the final chain as its local execution base.

transitions.label: Final execution hash differs
transitions.when: The bank is frozen and its block ID matches a final block, but its expected execution hash differs.
transitions.action: Stop the validator and save diagnostics.
transitions.why: The validator computed a different state for the block that the network finalized. It cannot safely continue from that state.

transitions.label: New final slot
transitions.when: Agave observes a new highest final slot.
transitions.action: Reset the ten-second standstill timer.
transitions.why: A new final slot is direct evidence that the network is making progress.

transitions.label: Ten seconds without progress
transitions.when: No new final slot appears for ten seconds.
transitions.action: Record slot f. Send stored votes above f and related certificates again.
transitions.why: Other validators can lack the evidence needed for the next decision.

transitions.label: Another ten seconds
transitions.when: The network still has no new final slot after the next interval.
transitions.action: Send the required votes and certificates again.
transitions.why: One retransmission can also be lost or arrive too late. Repetition gives recovery another opportunity.

transitions.label: New window needs a timer
transitions.when: Agave creates a timer while standstill is active.
transitions.action: Increase the network allowance according to the number of windows since f.
transitions.why: More time can prevent repeated skips when the earlier allowance was too short.

transitions.label: Timer created
transitions.when: The new timer has its adjusted network allowance.
transitions.action: Continue standstill monitoring. Keep the normal block and first-data intervals.
transitions.why: Creating a longer timer does not itself prove that final decisions have resumed.

transitions.label: A later slot is final
transitions.when: Agave observes a final slot above f.
transitions.action: Clear standstill and return to normal progress tracking.
transitions.why: The new final slot proves that the network has passed the point where progress stopped.
